meta.face: St. Joseph as on the `joseph` card, the same man: about sixty, with a LONG OVAL face — a high, domed, balding forehead with a few thin strands on top; thick, wavy silver-grey hair at the temples and the back, curling over the ears to the nape; a long, straight nose with a softly rounded tip; heavy-lidded, gentle eyes lowered toward the Child under softly arched grey brows; lean cheeks over moderate cheekbones; a full, neat, ROUNDED silver-grey beard and moustache covering the jaw; a small, tender smile; the head bowed in three-quarter view.
meta.basis: The same face as the `joseph` card (19 Mar), so that the patriarch is one man on both of his days: the older, balding, greying Joseph of 19th-century cards with the Painter's Manual's rounded beard. The scene is the carpenter's shop of Nazareth (Mt 13:55, quoted by the formulary), as painted by Georges de La Tour (Joseph boring a beam with an auger, the Child beside him) and taken up in the images of Joseph teaching Jesus his trade that followed Pius XII's institution of the feast on 1 May 1955; the lily is his traditional attribute.
